heading: Evaluating Client Attestation Failure Rates Under High-Volume Fraud Base Rates
core_technical_idea: Attestation relay attack architecture where hypervisor-controlled emulators delegate TEE hardware signing challenges to a cluster of physical devices
must_show: Target app running inside QEMU/KVM emulator
Physical rooted Android device executing TEE hardware key signing
Valid attestation token delivered back to application backend
composition: Horizontal sequence diagram flowing left-to-right from the emulated client environment through the kernel boundary, over the relay infrastructure to the physical TEE hardware, and back up to the verification backend.
alt_text: Sequence diagram illustrating an attestation relay attack flow where an emulator intercepts system calls and delegates hardware-backed attestation signing to a physical device with a real TEE.
caption: Attestation Relay Attack: How emulated clients bypass hardware root-of-trust by delegating TEE signing challenges to physical devices.
mermaid_code:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant App as Target App (Emulator)
    participant Kernel as Hypervisor / Custom ROM Kernel
    participant Relay as Attestation Relay Server
    participant PhysDevice as Physical Device (TEE)
    participant Backend as Application Server

    App->>Kernel: Request Attestation (keystore2 Syscall)
    Kernel->>Relay: Intercept & Forward Nonce Payload
    Relay->>PhysDevice: Push Signing Request to Device Pool
    PhysDevice->>PhysDevice: Hardware Keymaster Signs Nonce in TEE
    PhysDevice-->>Relay: Valid Certificate Chain + Signature
    Relay-->>Kernel: Return Signed Attestation Response
    Kernel-->>App: Deliver Valid Payload (MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY)
    App->>Backend: Submit API Request + Relay-Signed Payload
    Backend->>Backend: Verify Signature (Passes Root-of-Trust Check)

    A[Client Request] -->|TLS ClientHello| B(Network Edge / API Gateway)
